chapter: New Orleans, Havana and back to New York
title: Miami Beach gig at the Gangplank and fleeing his first wife to Havana
summary: Romer got him a five-piece job in Miami; newly married and sued for alimony, he fled by boat to Havana.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Did you have any association with him after he pulled that on you in New Orleans?

Yeah, he actually did get me a job, later that year, in Miami Beach, with a five piece band, at a place called The Gangplank. Oh, it was a horrible band. They used local Miami musicians, and the only note that came out of the bass player was the slap, and it was terrible. But he -- one thing that happened there, during that time, I had gotten married, and it didn't work, and my -- that was my first wife and she was after me, so I decided I'd better go to Cuba. And --
Did you get married in Miami?

No, I was married in New York. We went back to New York after the New Orleans fiasco. And I had gone to Florida and Milton had gotten me this job, and in the meantime, I had gotten married. So I get word she's coming, and I said, 'Well, I'm going to Cuba.' There was a boat, an overnight boat, that used to leave for Havana, right out of Miami Beach there, and as the boat's pulling out, here she comes with her process server and I'm on the stern of the boat, and I'm hollering at her, 'Millions for defense, but not one cent for alimony.' I stayed in Havana for, oh, about the better part of four months.
